info.title: dreamDEX
info.description:
The dreamDEX REST API served from the Somnia Markets stack — every response is derived from the on-chain order books and their indexer through @somnia-chain/markets-sdk.

Every operation answers `451` in plain text to a caller in a sanctioned region, and the operations tagged `Restricted` also answer it to a perp write from a perp-restricted region.

Rate limits: each request counts against exactly one bucket. A request with a valid bearer token counts per wallet, from any IP and on any endpoint (400 requests per second). Otherwise a `/v0/auth/*` request counts per client IP in the auth bucket (40 requests per second), and any other request per client IP in the general bucket, shared across every endpoint (200 requests per second). Health probes and allowlisted IPs are not limited. Each is a sliding one-second window, in which the previous second's count decays as the current one advances. Limits are counted by each server instance, so the ceiling across a deployment can be higher. A REST call over the WebSocket is counted as an HTTP request from the socket's IP would be. Past a limit the answer is `429` with `Retry-After: 1` and the plain-text body `rate limit exceeded`.

chainId.description: The chain this row is on. Ids are unique only within one chain, and symbols only within one chain and kind.

Symbol.description: Market symbol in `BASE:QUOTE` form using this exchange's currency codes (e.g. `SOMI:USDso`). `GET /v0/markets` is authoritative. A symbol is unique within one chain and kind, not across kinds: a spot and a perp market can share one. In a path it names the spot market unless `kind` selects another; with `symbols`, `kind=all` lists every market each symbol names. A spot or perp market's `contract` address is accepted wherever a symbol is and always names exactly one market; where a route also filters by `kind`, the kind must match. An event-contract market is `ASSET-N:QUOTE`, N its market number (e.g. `BTC-37305:USDso`); only live ones are listed there, under `kind=event`.

MarketKind.description: Class of a market. `spot` is an order-book spot market; `perp` is a perpetual-futures market; `event` is an event contract, a yes-or-no market that resolves at its expiry. Clients should treat unknown future values as forward-compatible rather than an error.

interval.description: The series cadence, e.g. `15m`. To follow an asset across rolls, read `GET /v0/markets?kind=event` and take the market with the same `asset` and `interval` whose `state` is `trading`; the next roll can be listed beside it as `listed`.

outcomes.description: ERC-6909 token ids of the two outcomes.

state.description: Derived from the trading window and resolution, not the indexed status, which lags.

outcome.description: The winning outcome. Absent on a void.

payout.description: What one token of each outcome pays, `[yes, no]` over `denominator`. A void pays per its stored vector.

resolution.description: Present once the market has resolved or voided.

MarketKindFilter.description: Market class to filter by. Defaults to `spot`. `event` lists live event contracts only; a past one is reachable by its symbol. With `symbols`, `all` returns every market each symbol names, so a symbol a spot and a perp market share gives two rows, told apart by `kind` and `contract`. The cross-market tape (`/v0/trades/all`) and the WebSocket feeds don't serve event contracts yet.

TickerInfo.description: Rolling 24-hour OHLCV statistics aggregated from one-minute candles. OHLCV is derived solely from trades, so a market with resting depth but no trades in the window reports "0" for every field - use `lastTradeAt` for freshness.

id.description: Trade id as `<block>_<logIndex>`, identical on REST and WS for the same trade. It differs from api.dreamdex.io's per-surface id shapes and is not preserved across the cutover — re-key stored ids (DEXSVC-191).

allOf.description: Collateral redeemable now, net of the settlement fee: the winning side once resolved, the stored payout once voided, `0` while trading.

EventPosition.description: An event-contract position, per outcome: a wallet can hold YES and NO at once, so the two books are never blended. Balances are outcome tokens; money fields are collateral; prices are per outcome token, so a leg's price is in its own outcome's terms.

post.description: `fundingSource` is validated against the market KIND — spot takes `wallet` or `vault`, perp requires `marginBank` — not against the wallet’s on-chain pool mode; it selects how a `market` order’s sweep is priced (below), while the wallet’s actual mode (spot auto-pull or manual vault, perp always the MarginBank) governs funding at execution and the pool resolves any mismatch. Returns the unsigned placement transaction. A `market` order is an immediate-or-cancel limit whose price is the sweep bound, because the book has no priceless order type: a sell is placed at one tick so it crosses every bid, a vault- or MarginBank-funded buy at the largest price whose product with the quantity fits in uint256 so it sweeps the whole ask side, and a wallet-funded buy at the best ask plus `slippageBps` (default 500) since auto-pull reserves price times quantity up front. Fills execute at the maker's price, so the bound does not change what a fill costs. `approval` names the allowance the pool needs before the placement can pull escrow. On an event-contract market, `outcome` is required and `side` and `price` are in that outcome's terms; the order is accepted only while the market trades, its expiry defaults to the market's, `fundingSource` must be `wallet` or absent, builder attribution is not yet available, a `market` order is priced off the best opposite level by `slippageBps` either way, and `approvalTransaction`, when present, is the unsigned allowance or ERC-6909 operator grant to send first.

get.description: The marked value of the traded book over time, window PnL, money-weighted return, traded volume and the fee saving against a centralized-exchange taker rate, computed from the wallet's own spot fills marked against candle closes. Fills whose direction is unknowable (the taker side not yet joined) are skipped rather than guessed, and figures are USD-denominated by treating the quote currency as a dollar. The `equity` series is the marked value of the traded spot book at each sample - a level, opening at the value carried into the window rather than at `0`. Event-contract holdings are not in it; `GetWalletEventPositions` serves them. It is the book, not the wallet: a token that arrived without a fill, and idle quote balance, are not in it, and a position the sample cannot price (no candle in the window, no last price) is valued at zero and so left out of the level. `pnl` is a separate quantity, the window profit and loss: its `buckets` are the first differences of cumulative PnL, and `totalUsd` is the window total, so the two series plot different curves and neither is derivable from the other. `equity[].valueUsd` is typed signed because it sums signed position value; it is non-negative for the long-only spot book served today, which is not a guarantee to hold a chart axis to.
